# Emaki [絵巻]{.hero-kanji}

::: {.shift .rise}
## From the IDE to the ADE

{{< include _shift-ide.html >}}

::: {.shift-words}
::: {.shift-label}
**IDE** integrated development environment
:::

An IDE is built for writing code by hand: many panels, a steep learning
curve, and real effort to set up. With agents, you write less code and run
fewer commands yourself, yet the editor still takes the middle of the
screen and most of your attention. The agent chat and git sit at the
edges, and there is no way to manage the agent's sessions at all.
:::

{{< include _shift-ade.html >}}

::: {.shift-words}
::: {.shift-label}
**ADE** agentic development environment
:::

Emaki, an agentic development environment, turns this around. The agent
chat is the main panel, rendered with care, and four panels open beside it
when you need them: files, outline, shell terminal and agent terminal.
Sessions are listed under their projects, where you can manage them and
keep them safe from automatic deletion.
:::

:::

::: {.band .rise}
## Get started

Download the app, install an agent, and you are ready. Git and the GitHub
CLI are optional, for version control from the window.

::: {.starts}

::: {.start}
### Download Emaki

For macOS, Windows and Linux.

{{< include _download-step.html >}}
:::

::: {.start}
### Install the agents

Emaki works with Claude Code and Codex.

::: {.start-links}
[Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code){.pill .i-claude}
[Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli){.pill .i-codex}
:::
:::

::: {.start}
### Git (optional)

Install Git and the GitHub CLI to commit, branch and push from Emaki.

::: {.start-links}
[Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads){.pill .i-git-branch .pill-git}
[GitHub](https://cli.github.com){.pill .i-github .pill-github}
:::
:::

:::

:::

::: {.band .rise}
## Main system

Sessions are listed and managed under their projects. The agent chat
takes the main space, rendered in high quality.
:::

::: {.cards .cards-2 .rise}

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="projects" aria-label="Emaki's sidebar lying flat: projects in rows, the open one with its sessions under it. The project under the pointer unfolds its sessions, and the rows below make room."}
:::
### [Projects](docs/projects.qmd)
Every folder you work in is a project, its sessions under it, from Claude
Code and Codex side by side. Each Claude Code session is copied before
anything reads it, so one the agent has deleted is still here, and
[⌘K]{.kbd} searches them all.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="chats" aria-label="Emaki's chat lying flat: the transcript, and the composer under it. With the pointer on the composer, the draft rises as a bubble and lands at the transcript's end."}
:::
### [Chats](docs/chats.qmd)
The transcript as it reads: prompts in bubbles, replies across, tool
calls as cards. Under it the composer, with attachments, `@` for a file,
`/` for a command, and the mode, model and effort a click away.
:::

:::

::: {.band .rise}
## Panels

The panels are hidden by default: essential, but used less often than
the chat. Files and outline open on the left, the two terminals on the
right.
:::

::: {.cards .cards-2 .rise}

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="files" aria-label="The files panel lying flat: the tree, and the file's pane beside it. The file under the pointer opens in the pane, drawn as its kind."}
:::
### [Files](docs/files.qmd) [⌘⇧F]{.kbd}
The project as a tree with git's marks, worked like a file manager.
Click a file and it opens beside the chat, drawn as its kind:
code, markdown, a table, a PDF, a picture. Commit, branch and push from
the same panel.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="outline" aria-label="The outline beside the chat, lying flat. The entry under the pointer scrolls the chat to its round."}
:::
### [Outline](docs/outline.qmd) [⌘⇧O]{.kbd}
A label for every prompt, a few words each, under a heading for each
day. Click one and the chat glides back to that round.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="shell" aria-label="A terminal standing up with three tabs. The tab under the pointer comes up, and its screen types itself in."}
:::
### [Shell Terminal](docs/shell.qmd) [⌘⇧S]{.kbd}
Your shell, opened in the project's folder, in tabs at the
chat's right. Paste a picture and it lands as the path of a
file.
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.fig data-figure="agent" aria-label="The chat and the agent's own terminal standing side by side. The step under the pointer stands out of both."}
:::
### [Agent Terminal](docs/agent.qmd) [⌘⇧A]{.kbd}
The session's own agent in its terminal, as it runs. Watch it work as
in the CLI, and type into it when it asks something the window has no
card for.
:::

:::
